findings.issue: Turbopack 'Module not found' on parent-relative imports was worked around with a jsconfig alias instead of diagnosed; no Next.js docs, web search, or skill was consulted during a 7-turn detour.
findings.suggestion: On framework-specific resolution failures, consult the Next 16 docs / Turbopack issue tracker before switching strategies; the alias is fine, but the undiagnosed quirk could recur (e.g., with the harness's own build).

findings.issue: pkill -f "next" / "next-server" matched the agent's own shell command line and killed it (exit 143) — and the mistake was repeated at turn 78 after being fully diagnosed at turn 68.
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID or port (fuser/lsof) or use patterns that can't match the invoking command's own argv.

findings.issue: Two edits attempted against lib/api.js based on a misremembered file state, both failing to apply.
findings.suggestion: Read or grep the target region before issuing an edit.

findings.issue: Rebuild, pkill, and server start chained into one command caused a stale-build confusion and a lost server process.
findings.suggestion: Separate build from restart and always start servers detached (setsid nohup) as done in turn 70.

findings.issue: One agent-browser call used the wrong command form ('viewport' vs 'set viewport') despite having just read --help.
findings.suggestion: Minor; the skills output ('agent-browser skills get core') it surfaced would have prevented it.

summary: An unusually disciplined session: the agent read the spec, tests, API, fixture overlay and all reference screenshots before coding, and the full acceptance suite passed on its first run. Verification was exemplary — three full green test runs including one after the final edit, screenshot comparison at two breakpoints, HTML probes, and pre-validated edge-case data. Waste is limited to ~12 turns across three small loops, the most avoidable being a twice-repeated pkill self-kill and a Turbopack quirk worked around rather than diagnosed.
